result.title: Can a Vision-Language Model Tune Clustering In Context?
result.summary: Clustering is a widely used unsupervised learning method, but selecting an appropriate algorithm and set of hyperparameters for a specific dataset can require many possible configurations and evaluations. In this work, we investigate whether a Vision-Language Model can instead visually evaluate clustering results and use those decisions to then tune an explicit clustering algorithm. We study this through three progressive experiments using Qwen3.5-27B and five controlled synthetic clustering scenarios. First, we test whether the VLM can distinguish the best clustering result from a pair of plots. Second, we test whether it can assign numerical scores to those plots where a higher score represents a better result. Finally, we use these judgments within an agentic loop in which the VLM scores a k-means clustering and proposes updated hyperparameters that may result in better clustering. Our exploratory results show that the VLM performs well when clear cluster structure is present, while struggling on more ambiguous and noisy settings. In the full agentic experiment, the VLM produces clustering configurations with silhouette scores relatively close to those of grid search and Bayesian optimization, while terminating in much fewer iterations. Overall, these results provide an initial proof of concept that VLM-based visual feedback can be used to autonomously tune an explicit clustering algorithm.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 Qwen3.5-27B 在五个合成聚类场景中做三项递进实验：从成对图中判别最优聚类、给聚类图打数值分数、再把该分数接入 agentic 循环以提出新超参数；结果显示清晰结构下判断可靠、噪声歧义场景较弱，最终配置的 silhouette 接近网格搜索与贝叶斯优化但迭代更少。
AI.relevance_reason: VLM 以可视化结果作为证据打分并驱动迭代与提前终止，可供核查视觉证据如何参与验证与 STOP 决策，但其状态仅为外部聚类配置、并非 latent 推理状态，与 LVR 的迁移联系仍属推测。
